checks: 16 MiB file / 4 KiB overwrite saves 64 KiB, shares 255 blocks; snapshot bytes remain unchanged
overwriting a block with identical bytes reuses its old payload
cross-block write and normal remount preserve byte-exact contents
truncate/grow, partial last blocks and zero-length files survive remount without resurrecting bytes
payload, manifest and block-map insertion failures roll back together; dirty content remains readable and retries
SIGKILL restores the last complete commit and retains immutable history
held deleted snapshot, trash restore and independent backup/import preserve shared blocks
format-3 migration preserves paths, attributes and bytes; injected failure restores original schema
invalid block mappings are rejected without automatic repair or erasure
scope: Foundation acceptance, not a native filesystem or cloud performance comparison. Bytes are inserted content payload, not physical disk writes.
